title: LAST-V2X: Language-Driven Adaptive Scenario Synthesis and Testing for Communication-Induced Failures in V2X Safety Applications

control_signal.value: Short free-form natural-language prompt describing environment, ego maneuver, surrounding vehicles, safety-critical interaction, and optionally a communication condition or fault.

control_mechanism.value: An LLM compiler turns the prompt into a typed scenario specification, checked for feasibility and grounded by retrieval (road graph, V2X and driver-behaviour knowledge), then run in CARLA with message faults; parameter search and LLM self-reflection revise ineffective tests.

base_model.value: LLM-orchestrated four-module pipeline (agent analysis, retrieval-augmented grounding, CARLA synthesis with V2X communication and fault injection, refinement); no trained generative traffic model described in packet.

datasets.value: No dataset; evaluation on generated scenes: 100-scene normal-traffic benchmark across six V2X applications and eight CARLA towns, a communication-fault suite extended to 50 scenarios for refinement.

metrics.value: Run-level classes ADMITTED, NON-ATTRIBUTABLE, CLEAN, GATED; conflict-gap change delta g; hazard slack, decision-epoch Age of Information; admitted failures, attribution rate, gate rejection rate, executions required.

controllability_evidence.value: Adaptive refinement raises admitted failures from 7 to 32; search finds failures in 23 of 43 targets (median 8 executions to first admission); LLM self-reflection rescues 8 targets, two beyond search reach.

stated_limitations.value: Communication and fault parameters are representative, not field-measured; V2X application logic is simplified; large-scale search used a simplified backend; fixed-time signals assumed.

notes: Targets communication-induced V2X failures rather than traffic-agent behaviour control; control is by text intent, not by steering a generative trajectory model. Date in packet is 2026 arXiv id.
